limitations: This does not reject the independently checkable policy component.

our_interpretation: The preceding sentences describe comprehensive alternatives: public-domain-only training or licensing the remaining material. Rejecting those alternatives does not mean rejecting every licensing agreement.
The firm component concerns OpenAI’s publicly expressed training policy. Public statements can establish that position without establishing private motives.
The payment allegation is expressly tentative. 'Apparently' must not become a categorical assertion that OpenAI paid nobody, or a firm commitment about some evaluator-selected proportion of its data.
The relevant period is January 8–10, 2024: the response discussed in the post through the post date. This is an ongoing policy claim, not a quarterly financial observation.
The compound claim cannot receive a firm truth verdict without supplying a commitment that the payment qualification leaves unspecified. Its firm policy component can nevertheless be examined.
This is a qualitative claim about copyright and training policy, not a claim specifying a financial metric.
criteria.support_condition: The firm policy component would be supported by contemporaneous statements advocating continued training on copyrighted material without requiring licenses for all of it. That alone cannot establish the whole compound claim: the payment allegation remains qualified by 'apparently'. No binary support condition is assigned to that qualification.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A contemporaneous commitment to use only public-domain or licensed training material would contradict the firm policy component. Individual paid licenses would qualify the payment inference but would not refute rejection of universal licensing. No binary contradiction condition is assigned to the unspecified strength of 'apparently'.
